He played [[college basketball]] for [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]]. ==Early life and high school career== Gravett was born in [[Anniston, Alabama]]. Due to his family having military backgrounds, he has lived in many states as well as abroad. He spent two years in Italy, and spent several summers in Germany. However, he was mainly raised in the city of [[Atlanta, Georgia]]. Gravett attended [[Robert S. Alexander High School]] in [[Douglasville, Georgia]]. As a senior, he scored a career-high 46 points in a state tournament semifinal loss. He was named the Georgia Class 4A Player of the Year by the [[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]], an All-Metro selection by the Atlanta Tipoff Club, and was picked to play in the GACA All-Star Game. Gravett originally signed with [[Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball|Gardner–Webb]] out of high school before deciding to do a prep year at the [[Hargrave Military Academy]]. He committed to [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|Louisiana-Lafayette]] in November 2014.{{cite news |last1=Buckley |first1=Tim |title=UL gets verbal commitment from shooting guard |url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2014/11/03/ul-gets-verbal-commitment-shooting-guard/18414323/ |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]] |date=November 3, 2014}} He later rescinded his commitment and decided to play at [[Pensacola State College]].{{cite web |last1=Hunte |first1=Sydney |title=JUCO guard Hassani Gravett commits to South Carolina Gamecocks basketball |url=https://www.garnetandblackattack.com/south-carolina-basketball/2016/4/18/11456246/hassani-gravett-south-carolina-gamecocks-basketball-frank-martin |website=GarnetandBlackAttack.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |date=April 18, 2016}} ==College career== Gravett dealt with injuries in his freshman season at Pensacola State and only played 12 of the final 14 games. He averaged 16.1 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game. On April 18, 2016, Gravett signed with [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], choosing the Gamecocks over offers from [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], [[St. Louis Billikens men's basketball|St. Louis]] and [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]].{{cite news |last1=Vilona |first1=Bill |title=Pensacola State wishes basketball season wouldn't end |url=https://www.pnj.com/story/sports/college/pensacola-state-college/2016/02/19/pensacola-state-wishes-basketball-season-wouldnt-end/80617256/ |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[Pensacola News Journal]] |date=February 19, 2016}} In his sophomore season at South Carolina, he helped the Gamecocks reach the Final Four.{{cite web |title=Representing USA Has Deeper Meaning for Hassani Gravett |url=https://medium.com/gamecocksonline-com/representing-usa-has-deeper-meaning-for-hassani-gravett-4c4d99f86e1c |website=[[Medium.com]] |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |date=September 29, 2017}} He averaged 3.2 points and 1.6 rebounds per game as a sophomore. As a junior, Gravett averaged 7.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game as South Carolina missed the postseason. In his senior season, the addition of transfer Tre Cambell and freshmen [[A. J. Lawson]] and T.J. Moss allowed Gravett to move to shooting guard, and he had 22 points in a win against [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite news |last1=Ramspacher |first1=Andrew |title=USC's season narrative is changing. So is the one around Hassani Gravett's career |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article224232895.html |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]] |date=January 10, 2019}} He was teased by the Florida student section for his hair, as they chanted "Blooming Onion".{{cite news |last1=Ramspacher |first1=Andrew |title=Like his hair, Hassani Gravett has bloomed for the Gamecocks this season |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article225392155.html |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]] |date=February 1, 2019}} Gravett started five of 32 games as a senior, averaging 11.4 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game, while shooting 39.9 percent from behind the arc and led the Gamecocks with 65 three-pointers. Gravett was named [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Sixth Man of the Year by the coaches. ==Professional career== [[File:Hassani Gravett and Lamar Peters.jpg|thumb|left|Gravett defending [[Lamar (2020–2021)=== On July 31, 2020, Gravett signed with [[KK MZT Skopje|MZT Skopje]] of the [[Macedonian First League (basketball)|Macedonian League]].{{cite web|title=Hassani Gravett joins MZT Skopje|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/ABA-League/news/638778/Hassani-Gravett-joins-MZT-Skopj|website=Eurobasket.com|date=July 31, 2020|access-date=July 31, 2020}} He averaged 12.4 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Ford, Gravett, Johnson and Schofield to 10-Day helped the team win the Macedonian League championship as well as the 2021 Macedonian Basketball Cup. ===Return to Lakeland (2021)=== On September 8, 2021, Gravett signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Jeff Dowtin, Hassani Gravett and Jon Teske|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jeff-dowtin-hassani-gravett-jon-teske-20210908|website=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=September 10, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 16.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-waive-four-players-20211016|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} Gravett subsequently rejoined the Lakeland Magic{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}} where he played 12 games and averaged 13.6 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.83 steals in 34.5 minutes. ===Orlando Magic (2021–2022)=== On December 17, 2021, Gravett signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]]. He signed a second 10-day contract with the team on December 27.{{cite news|date=December 27, 2021|title=Orlando Magic Sign Gravett and Schofield to Second 10-Day Contracts|work=[[NBA.com]]|agency=|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/national/story/2021-12-27/mondays-transactions|access-date=December 27, 2021}} ===Third stint with Lakeland (2022)=== On January 7, 2022, Gravett was reacquired by the [[Lakeland Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 7, 2022|access-date=January 7, 2022}} ===Memphis Hustle (2022)=== On August 25, 2022, Gravett was traded to the [[Windy City Bulls]],{{cite web |date=August 25, 2022 |title=G League transactions |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/transactions |access-date=August 25, 2022}} and on October 21, he was again traded to the [[Memphis Hustle]]. On November 4, Gravett was named to the opening night roster for the Hustle.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/memphis-hustle-announce-roster-moves-finalize-opening-night-roster/n-5895741|title=Memphis Hustle Announce Roster Moves; Finalize Opening Night Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} On November 16, he was waived after appearing in 3 games.{{Cite web |title=The Memphis Hustle today announced the team has waived guard Hassani Gravett. |url=https://twitter.com/memphishustle/status/1592978311394734080 |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=Twitter |language=en}} ===Raptors 905 (2022–2023)=== On November 26, 2022, Gravett was acquired by the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=November 25, 2022|access-date=November 25, 2022}} On January 25, 2023, Gravett was waived.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=January 25, 2023}} ===EWE Baskets Oldenburg (2023)=== On February 11, 2023, Gravett signed with [[Baskets Oldenburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/oldenburg-signs-shakur-juiston-and-hassani-gravett/|title=Oldenburg signs Shakur Juiston and Hassani Gravett|last=|first=|date=February 11, 2023|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 11, 2023|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Śląsk Wrocław (2023–2024)=== On July 18, 2023, Gravett signed with [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]] of the [[Polish Basketball League|PLK]].{{Cite web|url=https://wks-slask.eu/hassani-gravett-nowym-zawodnikiem-slaska/|title=Hassani Gravett nowym zawodnikiem Śląska|last=|first=|date=July 29, 2023|website=wks-slask.eu|publisher=|language=pl|access-date=July 29, 2023}} ===Indios de San Francisco de Macorís (2024)=== On June 29, 2024, Gravett signed with the [[Indios de San Francisco de Macorís]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].{{cite tweet|author=IndiosSFM ®|title=Anunciamos la contratación del jugador Hassani Gravett como nuestro nuevo refuerzo.
